summary: v67 Partner-led supplier onboarding + Commission Wallet. Backend: new pytest suite test_v67_partner_suppliers.py (33 tests, 32 pass) covers invite/list/403 for non-approved, CSRF, all 4 duplicate cases, before-consent blocks, public consent info/validation/accept/decline, partner edit-link/resume (editor=partner, 404 without cookie or with another partner's cookie), PATCH stripping decl_*/signature_* + partner_fields logging, partner doc upload logging, partner token cannot submit, send-for-review, supplier revoke (token stops working, edit-link 403), commission settings GET/PUT/validation, per-partner override + clear, approval accrues exactly one onboarding commission (not on re-approve, not when revoked), deal commission % and fixed, wrong-partner vendor_ref rejected (422), settle paid/void + second settle 409, admin & partner wallets totals, request-payout 200/409. Only failure: second consent response returns 404 not 409. Frontend (Playwright, 1920x1080): partner login -> /partner/me tabs, invite form + duplicate 409 toast, resend, fill (popup opens resume in partner mode with partner-edit-banner, save logs 1 edit), send-for-review updates stage; public consent page (accept disabled until all ticks+name, accept navigates to resume with partner-supplier-banner); supplier revoke via confirm -> access revoked & button hidden; admin /admin/e/partners commission-settings card save, partner detail wallet: suppliers list, deal form adds 10% commission, mark paid / void via window.prompt, totals update. All passed.

minor.issue: Returns 404 'invitation link is invalid or has expired' instead of 409 'already responded'. Cause: invite_decide sets partner_consent_token=None on accept/decline, so _by_consent_token can't find the reg and the 409 branch is unreachable. Fix: keep token (or store a used flag / partner_consent_used_token) and return 409, or accept 404 and update spec.

30-day claim has no practical effect: after another partner's claim expires (or is declined/revoked) the code still falls through to 409 'This supplier has already started a PMC registration' because the reg is still status=draft. A second partner can never take over an expired claim.

Deal commission is accepted for a supplier who REVOKED the partner's access (verified: 200 for revoked supplier vendor_ref). on_supplier_approved correctly skips onboarding for revoked, but deal path only checks partner_id+approved. Decide business rule (probably require partner_access=='granted').

Concurrent double-settle race: update_one filters status=due but modified_count is not checked, so two parallel requests could both return 200 and send two 'paid' emails. Check result.modified_count and 409 if 0.
Returns 422 (spec text said 'rejects' — fine, just noting status is 422 not 400/409).

ui_bugs.issue: Resend uses run() which always calls toast.success, so 'Email did not send' appears as a green success toast. Use toast.warning/error when email_sent=false.

Declaration checkboxes and signature fields are still shown/editable to the partner (SectionE has no editor==='partner' handling). Backend silently strips them, so the partner thinks they ticked/signed. Hide or disable decl_*/signature_* inputs when reg.editor==='partner' (verified by code; could not reach Section E in UI due to Section A format gate with seeded test data).

integration_issues.issue: Row stage label stays 'Ready to fill' after clicking Fill form until page reload (open() does not call reload()). Cosmetic.

issues: Incorporation date uses native browser date picker (mm/dd/yyyy) rather than shadcn calendar (pre-existing)

Hide/disable declarations + signature inputs in RegistrationResume Section E when editor==='partner'
Decide whether deal commissions are allowed for suppliers who revoked partner access; enforce in add_deal_commission
Fix claim-expiry logic in _dup_check so an expired/declined/revoked claim can be taken over (or document as permanent)
Check modified_count in settle_commission to prevent double settle race
Resend toast: show warning when email_sent=false
critical_code_review_comments: resolve_reg_token correctly ties partner_edit_token to partner cookie + partner_id + approved status; _out strips magic_token so partner never sees supplier's token — good.
update_draft public PATCH has no CSRF check but requires the partner_edit_token in the query, so cross-site forgery is not feasible; OK.

Partner can still overwrite document_slots dict via PATCH (pre-existing model allows it) — partner could point slots at arbitrary upload keys; consider stripping document_slots for editor=partner (uploads go via dedicated endpoint).
